bibl.title: Altars of Cleopatra VII and Ptolemy XV Caesarion at Teos.
bibl.seg: Christopher P. Jones, Altars of Cleopatra VII and Ptolemy XV Caesarion at Teos.
Philia. International Journal of Ancient Mediterranean Studies 6 (2020) pp. 85-92, figg.
bibl.note: An altar discovered during excavations at Teos in 2013 was erected by L. Munatius Apollonius for several deified Ptolemaic kings and a living king Ptolemy: it is similar in form and subject to the one bearing the names of three deified Ptolemaic queens and of a living queen Cleopatra. The dedicant is L. Munatius Apollonius, whose Roman citizenship is likely to go back to L. Munatius Plancus, a close supporter of Antony. Therefore the living king Ptolemy mentioned in the new altar can only be Ptolemy XV Caesarion, and both altars edited here were probably erected c. 33/32 BC, when Cleopatra and Caesarion visited Ionia alongside Antony before the battle of Actium.
